1	stories15M — a language model that carries its own engine
2	=========================================================
3	
4	This is a werk package: ONE FILE that carries an artifact and everything needed
5	to understand it. This particular one carries a language model, and "everything
6	needed to understand it" was taken literally.
7	
8	WHAT IS IN HERE
9	
10	  model/stories15M.bin       the weights. 15 191 712 parameters, f32, 58 MB.
11	  model/tokenizer.bin        the vocabulary. 32 000 entries.
12	  tools/llama2c/             the COMPLETE SOURCE of a runtime that runs it:
13	                             ~970 lines of C99, no dependencies, no build
14	                             system, no network.
15	  spec/layouts/              a byte-exact grammar for each of the two binary
16	                             formats above.
17	  testvectors/               what the model MUST produce, deterministically,
18	                             so you can tell "it ran" from "it ran correctly".
19	  spec/                      the werk format specification itself.
20	  loaders/                   three single-file, dependency-free readers for
21	                             this container: one Python, one Rust, one C.
22	  recipe/, disclosure/, provenance/, LICENSE
23	                             where the weights came from, what is model output
24	                             and what is not, and the three licences that meet
25	                             in this file.
26	
27	HOW TO GET TEXT OUT OF IT
28	
29	  1. Extract. It is a store-mode zip; any zip tool works, or use
30	     loaders/werk_read.py, which needs nothing but a Python interpreter.
31	  2. Read tools/llama2c/BUILD-AND-RUN.md. It has the exact compile command for
32	     each platform, says which of them were measured and on what machine, and
33	     says which one is upstream's and was not measured here.
34	  3. Build the runtime from source. There is no binary in this package.
35	  4. Run it. The invocation is in BUILD-AND-RUN.md §3 and in
36	     testvectors/vectors.json as an argv array.
37	  5. Check your output against testvectors/vectors.json. That step is the
38	     point of the package: a runtime that reads the weights at the wrong
39	     offsets still emits confident English, and only the vector catches it.
40	
41	NOTHING HERE RUNS ITSELF
42	
43	There is no compiled artifact anywhere in this package, and no werk tool
44	executes anything it finds in one. spec/SPEC.md §7.1 is the rule: source is
45	always allowed and reading it is the point; a prebuilt binary is inert data and
46	is never executed automatically under any circumstance, including a valid
47	signature. This package has no prebuilt binary at all, so every executable byte
48	you end up with is one you produced from source you can read.
49	
50	A NOTE ON THE PROFILE
51	
52	This package declares `profile: "model/1-draft"`. THAT PROFILE DOES NOT EXIST as
53	a ruled part of the werk specification. It was drafted while building this file,
54	because the file had nowhere to declare what it was, and the draft is carried
55	here at spec/PROFILE-MODEL-DRAFT.md together with the manifest schema it
56	validates against (spec/schemas/manifest.model-draft.schema.json). Section 5 of
57	the draft lists five places where the existing core doctrine does not fit a
58	model package — a missing `train` role, a hermeticity rule no model package can
59	satisfy, a disclosure axis that has one dimension where a model has two, a tool
60	role vocabulary with no word for "executor", and the absence of the node types
61	this package had to declare in the `x.` namespace. None of them are fixed. They
62	were found by building this, which is what fixtures are for.
63	
64	WHAT THIS PACKAGE IS NOT
65	
66	Not a benchmark: the test vectors check that execution is CORRECT, not that the
67	model is good. It is a 15 M-parameter story completer trained on a synthetic
68	children's-story corpus and it will happily contradict itself in the third
69	sentence.
70	
71	Not a training record: the weights are the output of a run this package did not
72	perform and cannot reproduce. recipe/recipe.json says so, in the format's own
73	vocabulary, with `reproducibility: "descriptive"`.
74	
75	Not fast: the carried runtime is scalar C on one core, measured at ~94 tokens
76	per second. Optimised executors are somebody's product and an extension-tier
77	concern by design; base doctrine's job is that a stranger can get output at all.

1	# BUILD AND RUN — the runtime this package carries
2	
3	This package contains a language model and the complete source of a runtime
4	that executes it. This file is the exact procedure: what to compile, with what
5	command, and what to run to get text out. Every command below is quoted as it
6	was actually typed; the ones marked **VERIFIED** were run by the package's
7	author on the machine described in §5 and their output is what
8	`testvectors/vectors.json` records.
9	
10	Nothing here is executed for you and nothing in this package executes itself.
11	`spec/SPEC.md` §7.1 is the rule and it is not softened here: source is always
12	allowed and reading it is the point; a compiled artifact is inert data. There is
13	no compiled artifact in this package — every executable byte you end up with,
14	you produced.
15	
16	## 1. What you need out of the package
17	
18	Extract the whole package (it is a store-mode zip; any zip tool, or the
19	zero-dependency reader in `loaders/`). Four paths matter:
20	
21	| path | what it is |
22	|---|---|
23	| `tools/llama2c/run.c` | the whole runtime, ~970 lines of C99, no dependencies beyond the standard library and libm |
24	| `tools/llama2c/win.h`, `tools/llama2c/win.c` | a Windows shim providing `mmap`/`munmap`/`clock_gettime`. Needed on Windows ONLY; `run.c` includes `win.h` behind `#if defined _WIN32` |
25	| `model/stories15M.bin` | the weights, 60 816 028 bytes, f32. Layout: `spec/layouts/llama2c-checkpoint.layout.txt` |
26	| `model/tokenizer.bin` | the vocabulary, 433 869 bytes. Layout: `spec/layouts/llama2c-tokenizer.layout.txt` |
27	
28	Toolchain: any hosted C99 compiler. Nothing is downloaded, nothing is
29	installed, there is no build system, no makefile is required and no network
30	access is needed at any point.
31	
32	## 2. Build
33	
34	Run these from the extracted package root.
35	
36	### 2a. POSIX — Linux, macOS, WSL, MSYS2's UCRT/MSYS shells
37	
38	```
39	cc -O3 -o run tools/llama2c/run.c -lm
40	```
41	
42	`win.c` is NOT compiled on POSIX and MUST NOT be: `run.c` takes the
43	`<sys/mman.h>` branch there. This is upstream llama2.c's own build line
44	(`gcc -O3 -o run run.c -lm`, from its README, which this package carries at
45	`recipe/inputs/llama2c-README.md`). **NOT VERIFIED HERE** — the machine in §5
46	is Windows and had no working POSIX C compiler on it, so this command is
47	reported as upstream's, unmeasured, and is labelled that way rather than
48	claimed. If it fails for you, that is a fact worth reporting; the two commands
49	below are the ones that were measured.
50	
51	### 2b. Windows, MSVC — **VERIFIED**
52	
53	From a shell where `cl.exe` is on PATH (run `vcvars64.bat` from your Visual
54	Studio installation first, or use a "x64 Native Tools Command Prompt"):
55	
56	```
57	cl /nologo /O2 /Fe:run.exe tools\llama2c\run.c tools\llama2c\win.c
58	```
59	
60	Both `.c` files. `win.c` supplies `mmap`, `munmap` and `clock_gettime`, which
61	`run.c` calls and which Windows does not have. Measured: exit 0, one warning-free
62	`Generating Code...`, a 218 624-byte `run.exe`.
63	
64	### 2c. Windows, mingw-w64 gcc — **VERIFIED TO FAIL, UNMODIFIED**
65	
66	```
67	gcc -O3 -o run.exe tools/llama2c/run.c tools/llama2c/win.c -lm
68	```
69	
70	does **not** build with mingw-w64 gcc 15.2.0. Measured, both errors, verbatim:
71	
72	```
73	win.c:136: error: passing argument 4 of 'VirtualProtect' from incompatible
74	           pointer type   (uint32_t * vs PDWORD, i.e. unsigned long *)
75	win.c:175: error: redefinition of 'clock_gettime'
76	           (mingw's own <pthread_time.h> already defines it inline)
77	```
78	
79	Neither is a werk problem and neither is fixed here, because fixing it would
80	mean shipping a `win.c` whose bytes are not the ones its author published — and
81	then this package's `sha256` for that file would no longer match upstream, which
82	is the one property that lets a stranger check where the code came from. The
83	two changes a consumer needs, if a mingw build is what they want, are one cast
84	and one `#if !defined(__MINGW32__)` guard, both inside `win.c`, both outside the
85	scope of this package. Use §2b instead.
86	
87	Suppressing the first error with `-Wno-incompatible-pointer-types` and renaming
88	the second with `-Dclock_gettime=...` was also tried, and also fails: the rename
89	applies to mingw's own inline definition too. Recorded so nobody spends the
90	twenty minutes again.
91	
92	## 3. Run
93	
94	```
95	./run model/stories15M.bin -z model/tokenizer.bin -t 0.0 -n 64 -i "Once upon a time"
96	```
97	
98	(on Windows, `run.exe model\stories15M.bin -z model\tokenizer.bin -t 0.0 -n 64 -i "Once upon a time"`)
99	
100	Flags that matter:
101	
102	| flag | meaning |
103	|---|---|
104	| first positional | path to the checkpoint. Required. |
105	| `-z <path>` | tokenizer path. **Required here**, because run.c's default is `tokenizer.bin` in the CURRENT DIRECTORY and this package puts it in `model/`. Omitting it is the single most likely way to fail. |
106	| `-t <float>` | temperature. **`-t 0.0` selects greedy argmax and makes the run deterministic.** Any other value samples and the output will not match the test vectors. |
107	| `-n <int>` | number of steps. |
108	| `-i <string>` | the prompt. |
109	| `-s <int>` | RNG seed. Irrelevant at `-t 0.0`; the sampler is never consulted. |
110	
111	The generated text goes to **stdout**. A timing line (`achieved tok/s: …`) goes
112	to **stderr** and is not part of any test vector.
113	
114	## 4. Check your result against the package
115	
116	`testvectors/vectors.json` is the correctness anchor. It records, for two
117	temperature-0 runs, the exact command line, the exact stdout, its sha256, and
118	the exact sequence of token ids. Verify like this:
119	
120	1. Run the command in `vectors[i].argv`.
121	2. Take stdout, **replace CRLF with LF**, and compare against
122	   `vectors[i].stdout_text` — or hash it and compare against
123	   `vectors[i].stdout_sha256_lf`.
124	3. It should match byte for byte.
125	
126	The CRLF normalisation is not a fudge. `run.c` writes to a text-mode stream, so
127	the newlines inside the generated story come out as `\n` on POSIX and `\r\n` on
128	Windows from an identical model computation. The hash is therefore declared over
129	the LF form and the byte count of the LF form is given too
130	(`stdout_bytes_lf`). The raw Windows-console hash of the first vector is
131	recorded separately as `stdout_sha256_crlf` so that the normalisation can itself
132	be checked rather than taken on trust.
133	
134	`vectors[i].token_ids` is the stronger anchor: token ids are integers and no
135	newline convention touches them. They were captured by a two-line
136	instrumentation of `run.c`, and that instrumentation travels in this package as
137	`testvectors/tokens_instrumentation.diff` so you can reproduce the capture
138	instead of believing it. **The unmodified `run.c` does not print token ids** —
139	matching `stdout_sha256_lf` is the check you can do without patching anything,
140	and it is sufficient.
141	
142	### If it does not match
143	
144	Floating-point summation order is the expected cause and it is a real one: the
145	runtime is scalar C, but a compiler is free to vectorise the reductions in
146	`rmsnorm`, `softmax` and `matmul`, and `-ffast-math` or an aggressive `-O` on a
147	different target will reassociate them. A greedy argmax over 32 000 logits is
148	usually robust to that, and it is not guaranteed to be. So:
149	
150	* a run that matches **is** strong evidence the whole chain is right;
151	* a run that **diverges after N tokens** is evidence of arithmetic reassociation,
152	  not necessarily of a broken reader. Report N and your compiler flags.
153	* a run that produces **fluent English but a different story from token 1** means
154	  the prompt encoding differs — check §5 of the tokenizer layout grammar (the
155	  BOS token and the dummy-prefix space).
156	* a run that produces **garbage from token 1** means the weights are being read
157	  at the wrong offsets — check the dead RoPE tables in §4 of the checkpoint
158	  layout grammar.
159	
160	## 5. The machine the vectors were produced on
161	
162	Recorded because "it matched" is only a measurement if you know against what.
163	
164	| | |
165	|---|---|
166	| OS | Microsoft Windows 10 Enterprise, 10.0.19045, x64 |
167	| CPU | AMD Ryzen Threadripper 3970X (32 core) |
168	| compiler | Microsoft (R) C/C++ Optimizing Compiler Version **19.38.33143** for x64 (Visual Studio 2022 Community) |
169	| build command | `cl /nologo /O2 /Fe:run.exe run.c win.c` |
170	| binary | `run.exe`, 218 624 bytes |
171	| throughput | 93.75 tok/s on vector 1, 94.51 tok/s on vector 2 (from the runtime's own stderr line) |
172	
173	No GPU is involved anywhere. This is a 15 M-parameter model in f32 on one CPU
174	core.
175	
176	## 6. What this package does NOT contain
177	
178	Stated so nobody looks for it:
179	
180	* **no training code and no training data.** The weights are the output of a
181	  training run this package did not perform and cannot reproduce.
182	  `recipe/recipe.json` records what is known about that run — the architecture,
